item.title: At least 31 killed in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns on busy highway
item.description:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry. item.description:

It’s what you’ll hear if you watch any cable news segment on the topic. item.title: FedEx plane overshoots runway at Miami airport on Thanksgiving eve
item.description:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a ground stop at Miami International Airport Wednesday evening due to a disabled FedEx aircraft after it overshot the runway, disrupting flights amid the busy Thanksgiving holiday travel rush. Video from the scene shows a large FedEx cargo jet sitting near a fence that runs next to a busy road. The airport confirmed the aircraft overran Runway 26R, prompting all runways to close except for Runway 9R. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the airport and reported no injuries. The incident comes nearly three months after a Prime Air cargo jet overran Runway 30 at Miami International Airport, killing five people. item.title: Iraqi court sentences 8 French nationals to life in prison for IS group membership
item.description:
When you speak with him, Richard Daniel keeps using the words "grateful" and "blessing." A judge freed the 44-year-old Miami man from federal prison in 2024 after Daniel served 22 years of a 60-year mandatory minimum sentence. Since then, Daniel has seen divine providence everywhere in his life, from the mundane to the extraordinary. He says it's a blessing to run errands for his elderly mother on Saturdays and that it was a blessing when he hit two jackpots on the same slot machine last winter, winning roughly $40,000. The money allowed him to buy a car and rent an apartment of his own, a short walk from his mom's place in the same complex. item.title: California warns of flooding as King Tides peak over Thanksgiving
item.description:
Beaches close as Los Angeles and La Jolla see all-time high tides and big waves batter landmark pier in Pacifica Super El Niño weather brought record-breaking high tides up and down the California coast on Wednesday, sending seawater rushing into beachside communities and flooding roads and businesses. As big waves battered the coast, the tip of a landmark pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, was slammed into the sea, local news outlets reported . The pier, which had once housed a favorite local cafe , had previously suffered structural damage and had been closed to the public, the San Francisco Chronicle reported , and collapsed after contact with ocean swells 12 times stronger than on an average November day. item.title: Photos: Storms and an El Nino-charged king tide batter California’s coast
item.description:
California spent two months preparing for El Niño. This week, as king tides and a powerful Thanksgiving winter storm batter the coast, the state will find out if it is ready. In September, Gov. Gavin Newsom proclaimed a state of emergency for El Niño. In the proclamation and subsequent executive orders , he directed agencies to speed up permits, move supplies and people and suspend some of the state’s own rules. The state Office of Emergency Services and Department of Water Resources asked operators of levees and dams to inspect facilities ahead of the storm. The state agencies prepared sandbags, portable flood barriers and materials for emergency repairs. The state is also deploying swiftwater rescue vehicles, boats and other specialized equipment.
